title: Canonical publication observables corpus (RUB-922 / C01), schema version 1
description: Machine contract for conformance/fixtures/protocol/canonical_pipeline_v1.json, the sole external authority for canonical-pipeline results and effects. It constrains observable old-or-new publication, exact first-error and result identity, bounded resource outcomes and effect counts, and never names a mutex, an internal struct or a client-private type. An omitted optional row field states no expectation: it is neither a zero nor a wildcard match. Ordered sequences carried as strings list their elements in document order, separated by ', ' (or by '; ' where an element itself contains a comma).

authority.description: Provenance of every expected value: the architecture parent as superseded, the pinned normative spec and repository baselines, the executors that may consume this artifact, and the frozen consume direction. Expected rows are authored architecture authority; the generator never calls a node production path to compute one.

result_taxonomy.description: The closed result taxonomy. Every observation row result is a member name, optionally followed by its exact parenthesized argument.

coverage_receipt.description: Generated definition receipt mapping every enumerated class (closed result taxonomy plus every named observable, accepted, rejected and hostile bullet of RUB-922) to the row ids that define it; it records which rows freeze each class, not that each class is runtime-compared — only kind=observation rows are compared, so a class whose only carriers are authority/forbidden rows has no C01 runtime comparison (kind-aware split is RUB-1204). A class mapping to no row is a generation failure, never a corpus state.

kind.description: Acceptance semantics: only kind=observation rows are adapter-emitted and enter the RUB-926/RUB-901 record-ID union (their id is the consumers' row_id); authority and forbidden rows are static authority read directly and are never emitted or compared as records.

canonical_counters.description: Exact planner-owned canonical counter deltas as exact decimal or symbolic tokens, for example '+1', '0' or '+connect_count'. '+connect_count' resolves to the number of newly canonical connect rows in the plan the consumer itself constructs for the row, never to a value read back from client output.

effects.description: `order` is the normative ordering specification of the named effect boundaries — not a count: an observed sequence MUST equal it element for element, including a boundary that makes no attempt (e.g. block inventory relay without section-19 authority), which keeps its position rather than being omitted. `block_seen`/`evicted_block_seen` are transition tokens for the row's block hash (`evicted_block_seen`: for the evicted row's hash): `set` (unset→set), `cleared` (set→unset), `unchanged` (before equals after, either value); the precondition value lives in `scenario`. `canonical_da_sets_consumed` is a symbolic-token count in the `canonical_counters` grammar ('0', '+included_matching_sets'), never a JSON integer; `+included_matching_sets` is the number of exact included-matching retained COMPLETE_SET records removed, deduplicated by `set_identity` across the full plan, resolved by the consumer from the row's `scenario`.

detail.description: Static authored authority for the row. Adapters do not emit it and comparators do not compare it; every adapter-emitted disposition lives in a typed row field or in effects.

pending_owner.description: NORMATIVE ACCEPTANCE SEMANTICS. A row carrying pending_owner names the RUB issue that must deliver the machinery the row describes. Until that issue is Done the row is excluded from the RUB-926 zero-mismatch acceptance comparison and from RUB-901 Go-versus-Rust equality: for an observation row an adapter MUST still emit whatever it observes and a comparator MUST NOT report the row as a mismatch; on an authority or forbidden row the field is a provenance marker only, since that kind is never emitted or compared. When the named issue is Done the field is removed by a C01 revision and an observation row becomes gate-bearing. Only RUB-922 (C01) may add, change or remove this field; a consumer that mutates it is out of contract.
